result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and vehicle traffic signals. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and greenery, and utility poles create minor obstructions on the walkway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located within the sidewalk path, narrowing the effective width for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian walk/don't-walk signals are visible at the intersection, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve crossing safety and predictability.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and moving traffic.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and traffic signals. However, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signal heads and features a large building at the corner that may restrict sightlines for turning vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, requiring pedestrians to interpret vehicular signals which may not provide sufficient crossing or clearance intervals.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: The large stone building is positioned close to the property line at the corner, potentially blocking visibility between pedestrians and approaching or turning motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Far left corner of the intersection

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve clarity and safety for people crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Modify signal timing to provide a 3-7 second head start for pedestrians before the parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with essential pedestrian infrastructure, including marked crosswalks, curb ramps with tactile paving, and pedestrian signals. While the environment is functional, it lacks physical buffers such as street trees or bollards to separate pedestrians from the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of physical buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation such as trees, bollards, or planters between the sidewalk and the travel lanes.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line on the right side of the image

hazards.name: Wide corner radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry may encourage higher vehicle turning speeds, increasing risk during crossings.
hazards.location_in_image: The corner of Somerset St and Frankford Ave in the foreground

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing parallel line markings to continental or ladder style for better driver awareness.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Green Infrastructure
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical buffer and improve the pedestrian experience.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and paved sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure is present, the open geometry and lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions may allow for higher vehicle turning speeds.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing exposure
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross two lanes of traffic without a median or refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the zebra markings

hazards.name: Wide turning radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry lacks physical narrowing, which can encourage higher vehicle speeds during right turns.
hazards.location_in_image: Right corner near the traffic signal pole

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle green light.
